summary: Robust ANSWER extraction and enhanced prompts for consistency across task types

edits.hypothesis: Explicit ANSWER line extraction ensures consistent, parseable output format regardless of the model's full response, improving robustness for the grader across all task types
edits.targets_mode: Output format robustness and grader compatibility
edits.why_not_lower_lever: Output parsing requires control flow changes in the harness execution path; prompt adjustments alone cannot enforce the grader's format expectations once the model responds
edits.trigger_condition: Always: every response is scanned for ANSWER: prefix
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) Both passing tasks include ANSWER lines and would continue to pass; the extraction would return 'ANSWER: 42' and 'ANSWER: -114' respectively; (preservative) Fallback to last line preserves behavior when no ANSWER line exists, preventing regressions on novel formats; (transfer) Answer extraction is task-type agnostic and works for arithmetic, multiple choice, yes/no, counting, and sequences
edits.regression_risk: Minimal: only changes which line is returned, not the content; model already produces ANSWER lines in both test cases
edits.mechanism: Explicit ANSWER line extraction ensures consistent, parseable output format regardless of the model's full response, improving robustness for the grader across all task types

edits.hypothesis: Explicit system-level guidance on consistent formatting and step-by-step thinking encourages reliable ANSWER-line output and structured reasoning across all task types
edits.why_not_lower_lever: This is system-prompt guidance where prose is the right lever: explicit formatting rules and behavioral expectations directly influence model output structure
edits.trigger_condition: Always: system prompt applies to every task
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) Both tasks already demonstrate the requested behavior (step-by-step thinking, ANSWER lines), so the instructions align with observed output; (preservative) Guidance reinforces existing good patterns rather than changing them; (transfer) General formatting rules apply uniformly across all reasoning task types
edits.regression_risk: Low: reinforces patterns already demonstrated in passing traces
edits.mechanism: Explicit system-level guidance on consistent formatting and step-by-step thinking encourages reliable ANSWER-line output and structured reasoning across all task types

edits.hypothesis: Task-level prompt clarifying step-by-step decomposition and explicit answer format improves consistency and clarity, generalizing beyond single task types
edits.targets_mode: Problem-solving structure and output format clarity
edits.why_not_lower_lever: Task-level instructions are the right prose lever for setting expectations about problem-solving approach and output format for individual tasks
edits.trigger_condition: Always: task prompt applies to every task
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) Both passing tasks already solve step-by-step and include ANSWER lines, matching the requested format; (preservative) Clearer instructions support and reinforce the observed successful pattern; (transfer) General decomposition guidance applies to arithmetic, multiple choice, yes/no, counting, and sequence tasks
edits.regression_risk: Low: requested behavior matches observed behavior in both passing test cases
edits.mechanism: Task-level prompt clarifying step-by-step decomposition and explicit answer format improves consistency and clarity, generalizing beyond single task types

mechanism: Robust ANSWER extraction and enhanced prompts for consistency across task types
targets_mode: Output format robustness and grader compatibility, Output consistency and problem decomposition, Problem-solving structure and output format clarity
